title: unify terraform private state layout: gpu node pools, iam roles, networking migration
author: Jordan Lee
description: Motivation: unify the Terraform state layout used by Private deployments across GPU node pools, IAM roles, and networking modules to simplify upgrades, reduce state drift, and enable safer rollouts for on-prem / VPC customers. This PR introduces a compatibility migration path and new module interfaces so existing customers can opt-in to the new layout with a controlled plan/apply. Scope: modules/gpu-node-pool, modules/iam, modules/networking, modules/state-layout, example upgrade scripts, and CI plan verification. Checklist: - [x] New state layout RFC implemented (see internal doc: https://linear.app/ENG/issue/ENG-1023) - [x] Backwards-compatible migration helpers in modules/state-layout - [x] Add explicit IAM role bindings for Dedicated/Private workloads - [x] Update GPU node pool module to accept consolidated labels and taints schema - [x] Add example upgrade plan and rollback guidance in examples/private/upgrade-migration.md - [x] Add tflint/terraform fmt checks and CI plan validation Notes: the description below includes the high-level migration steps and decisions; the full rationale is in the linked Linear ticket. Migration summary: - Introduces modules/state-layout to centralize state key naming and remote state mapping. - GPU node pool module now exposes node_pool_id and instance_profile outputs to avoid importing computed names during migration. - IAM module adds explicit role resources and a bindings map to re-create stable role ARNs across state moves. - Networking module exposes vpc_name and route_table_id outputs and tolerates pre-existing resources via "import_if_exists" flags. Compatibility strategy: 1) Add the new modules and outputs without removing old resources (this PR). 2) Run the provided `examples/private/plan-migration.sh` to generate a plan that moves the state keys (manual verification recommended). 3) Apply the migration in a canary VPC, validate node pools come up and workloads pass smoke tests, then roll forward. Rollback strategy: keep previous state layout in place until the migration is manually promoted; examples include re-binding remote state and re-importing resources. Risks and mitigations: - Risk: IAM role ARN churn during state move. Mitigation: role resource is created with stable name and bindings map; example rollback steps included. - Risk: transient downtime while re-creating node pool resources. Mitigation: canary-first rollout and careful use of `create_before_destroy` where possible. Related PRs: pr-103221 (docs), pr-112300 (console observability hooks).

release_notes:
- Introduce unified state-layout module for Private deployments to centralize remote state naming and mappings.
- GPU node pool module: stable outputs, safer rename/migration path.
- IAM module: explicit role bindings and stable naming to reduce ARN churn during state moves.
- Networking module: additional outputs and import_if_exists flags to support existing VPCs.
- Example migration guide and plan script added for on-prem/VPC customers.
notes: This migration has been validated in staging and an internal canary. Operators should follow examples/private/upgrade-migration.md and run the plan with the provided scripts. For large fleets, we recommend the canary->batch->global rollout documented in the Linear ticket ENG-1023.
